subject: general
question: What does the passage mean when it states that social media acts as a "digital agora"?

options.text: It operates as an exclusive, private network for coordinated grassroots movements.
It functions as a strict regulatory body that fact-checks political leaders in real-time.
It serves as an open, public space for participatory dialogue and civic engagement.
It acts as an editorial filter that decides which news stories are allowed to go viral.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***A) It operates as an exclusive, private network for coordinated grassroots movements.***

 
 
• This **cannot be inferred**. The passage emphasizes openness and public participation, not exclusivity.
 
 
 
• ***B) It functions as a strict regulatory body that fact-checks political leaders in real-time.***
 
 
• This **cannot be inferred**. The passage does not describe social media as a regulatory authority.
 
 
 
• ***C) It serves as an open, public space for participatory dialogue and civic engagement.***
 
 
• This **can be inferred**. The passage explicitly compares social media to a "digital agora," meaning a public forum where citizens engage in dialogue, similar to ancient town halls or print columns.
 
 
 
• ***D) It acts as an editorial filter that decides which news stories are allowed to go viral.***
 
 
• This **cannot be inferred**. The passage highlights that social media bypasses editorial filters, allowing direct communication and grassroots mobilization.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3: It serves as an open, public space for participatory dialogue and civic engagement.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because social media is described as open and public, not exclusive.
 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because social media is not a regulatory body.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because the passage emphasizes bypassing editorial filters, not enforcing them.
